summary.headline: Astrology, Astrolabes, and Eclipse Omens
summary.text: Catalogue entries for folios 307v–329v of a Venetian manuscript, covering planetary hours and effects, geomantic signs, Manuel Komnenos’s defense of astrology, Isaac Argyros’s astrolabe construction, star diagrams, and John the Grammarian’s treatise on the astrolabe. The entry for Marcianus 334 describes its fourteenth-century scribes and defective index, then lists chapters on lunar epochs, eclipse and comet colors, and solar-eclipse effects attributed to Ptolemy.
